notes.text: For more than 8, the soup needs a very big pot, at least 8 quarts. Cook the sandwiches in two skillets side by side to save time.

callback.body: You've simmered a pot of vegetables before: small, lazy bubbles that cook things gently. The soup simmers the same way, all by itself, while you learn today's new move at the sandwich pan.

move.title: Golden outside, melted inside
move.body: Heat control means choosing how hot the pan is, and changing it when the food tells you to. Today you'll cook grilled cheese sandwiches over medium-low heat so the bread turns golden just as the cheese melts. A smooth tomato soup simmers on the next burner for dipping.

why.title: The bread and the cheese race
why.body: The bread touches the pan, so it browns fast. The cheese in the middle only gets the heat that travels through the bread, so it melts slowly. On high heat the bread wins: black outside, cold cheese inside. On medium-low, they finish together.

why.title: A lid traps heat
why.body: Covering the pan keeps hot air around the sandwich, so the cheese warms from the top as well as the bottom. That gives the cheese a head start while the first side browns.

why.title: Butter on the outside
why.body: Butter spread to the edges touches every part of the pan, so the whole slice browns evenly instead of in patches. Soft butter spreads thin without tearing the bread.

why.title: Simmering tames the tomatoes
why.body: Tomatoes straight from the can taste sharp and sour. Twenty minutes at a gentle simmer softens that sharp taste, cooks the onion into the soup, and lets the flavors blend into one. A pinch of sugar helps smooth out the sour too.

wrong.sign: The bread is dark but the cheese hasn't melted
wrong.fix: Turn the heat down, flip it, put the lid on, and give it another minute or two. Start the next batch on lower heat.

wrong.sign: The bread is pale and soft after the timer
wrong.fix: Turn the heat up a notch and keep going. Lift a corner every 30 seconds to check.
Add another pinch of sugar and a pinch of salt, stir, and taste again.
Stir in a splash of broth or water until it's how you like it.

quiz.q: Your grilled cheese is burning on the outside and the cheese is still cold. What went wrong?
quiz.explain: On high heat the bread browns before the heat reaches the cheese. Medium-low lets them finish together.

quiz.q: Why does the soup simmer for 20 minutes?
choices: To soften the sharp taste of the tomatoes
quiz.explain: Gentle simmering mellows the sour taste and blends the flavors.

substitutions.note: Gluten-free bread browns faster. Check the bottom a minute early.

steps.text: Take the sandwich butter out of the fridge and leave it on the counter, so it's soft by the time you need it.
Chop the onion into rough pieces. They don't need to be neat, because the soup gets blended smooth later. Peel the garlic and chop it small.
steps.tip: Hold the food with your hand shaped like a claw: fingertips tucked under, knuckles in front.

steps.text: Melt the soup butter with the olive oil in the large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook, stirring now and then, until it's soft.
steps.look: The onion is soft and see-through, with no dark brown edges.

steps.text: Add the garlic and stir for about a minute, until you can smell it.
steps.tip: Garlic burns fast. As soon as it smells good, move on.

steps.text: Pour in the crushed tomatoes and the broth. Add the sugar, {qty:salt} salt, and the pepper. Turn the heat up until it bubbles, then turn it down so it simmers. Set the lid on the pot slightly crooked, leaving a gap.
steps.tip: Tomato soup spits as it bubbles. The lid keeps it off you and the stove, and the gap lets steam out.
steps.look: Small, lazy bubbles. Stir it every few minutes so nothing sticks to the bottom.

steps.text: While the soup simmers, make the sandwiches. Spread a thin layer of soft butter on one side of every slice of bread, all the way to the edges. Lay half the slices butter side down on a clean plate or the counter, put 2 slices of cheese on each, and top with another slice, butter side up.
Heat the skillet over medium-low heat.
Lay 2 sandwiches in the pan. Cover with the lid and cook until the bottoms are golden brown.
steps.look: Lift a corner with the spatula: even golden brown, like toast.

steps.text: Flip each sandwich with the spatula. Leave the lid off and cook until the second side is golden and the cheese is melted.
steps.look: Cheese starting to ooze out at the edges.

steps.text: Move the sandwiches to the cutting board and cook the rest the same way, 2 at a time.
steps.tip: The pan gets hotter with each batch. If a sandwich browns too fast, turn the heat down a little and check a minute sooner.

steps.text: Turn off the soup and take off the lid. Let it cool for 5 minutes. Then blend it with the stick blender until smooth, keeping the blade all the way under the soup the whole time.
steps.tip: Put the blender in the soup before you switch it on, and switch it off before you lift it out. Otherwise it sprays hot soup.

steps.text: Stir in the milk if you're using it. Taste the soup on a clean spoon, after letting it cool, and add a pinch more salt if it needs it.
Cut each sandwich in half from corner to corner. Ladle the soup into bowls, tear a few basil leaves on top if you're using them, and dip away.
steps.tip: Fill bowls on the counter next to the stove, not over the burner.
